en: to the house, too! You'll always be welcome.

en: I'm sorry, Darrell.
What I'm about to do will tear you away
from your wife, I suppose
note: followed by #152 '...'; cut matches the JP (#1202 ends mid-sentence)

en: But this is the only thing I can do.

en: I must do something, and quickly
I have been awaiting you.
Ugh... My joints ache...
Guess there's no beating old age, eh?
, my master. Give me any order you wish...
note: after the name; same wording as #854 ', my master.' + #855 'Give me any order you wish'

en: In my youth I'd fall off coaches and get hurt.
But lately I've always got fresh cuts. Odd, eh?
How about it, want a ride?
We'll be setting off soon.
No, I can walk there.
That won't be necessary.
note: shared with Arthur msg 193722 (player declines a wig, then 'I like my hair as it is'); stern register

en: Is that so? Well, suit yourself.
Still, going on foot... I admire that.
Folks today, it's all trains and motorcars
Well, they are convenient, admittedly.
Don't make me laugh! Those things
spew smoke all over the place.
With contraptions like that tearing about,
old Tom here is going out of business.
Well, see you, sir. It's time to set off.
Whenever you need a ride, come see me.
Oh, it's you. How about it, want a ride?
The coach will be setting off soon.
Well, they do seem convenient.
Ride with me next time. I'll be waiting.
Hey, back again, are you?
Well, why not stay and chat a while?
Mind you, it's just me grumbling.
There are lots more motorcars in town lately.
They race about spewing odd smoke.
It galls me, but they're fast and handy, sure.
Maybe my day has come and gone.
note: follows #152 '...' directly (no pause): '...Maybe my day has come and gone.'

en: Are coaches like mine doomed to vanish?
Hey, we meet again.
I don't know if it's admirable, but you always
get around on foot, eh? Doesn't it tire you?
Sigh... If you've got a moment, hear me out.
Fewer folks go out by coach these days.
So I spend more time just idling like this.
And my son won't take over the trade, I bet.
Sort of a lonely story, isn't it
How are you doing?
Lots of fares today, so I'm in a good mood.
Hope you have a good day too. See you.
Even if coaches die out one day,
this is my job, and I'll see it through.
Hm? What's the matter?
Sorry, there are no coaches at this hour yet.
If there's no rush, come back a bit later.
Not yet, not yet! Wait a little longer, I said.
Oh, it's you. Honestly, you're a handful.
I'm off work at this hour, you know.
Best remember that, or you'll lose out.
Well, well, well, you're an impatient one.
Or have you got something to talk about?
I didn't get old for nothing. Shall I listen?
Oh, I had a feeling you'd come.
Go on, ride the coach once in a while.
When it's empty, I'll take you for free.
Mind you, the free ride's a one-time offer.
Come again. I'll keep you company.
No, thank you. I can walk, so I'll be fine.
I'm sorry, but I'll have to decline.
Well, they are very handy, after all.
Well, see you, mate. It's time to set off.
They race about spewing weird smoke, see.
So I spend ever more time idling like this.
My son likely won't take on the trade, either.
After that, you pay.
Tom
You work so hard every day... I'm sorry.
Ah
